as_told.title: Geological paper on hydrocarbon seepages under Giza

plain: A scientific paper is said to show that a karst system under the Giza Plateau in Egypt, home of the great pyramids, is the source of hydrogen sulfide gas rising from the ground. Karst means a network of caves and tunnels worn into limestone. A researcher, named Jeffrey Drum in one episode and Geoffrey Drumm in another, describes the paper on an episode about an energy grid he believes lies beneath the pyramids. In the later episode he reads out its full title: "The development of sulfuric acid speleogenetic deposits within cavernous Middle Eocene beds and inference on hydrocarbon gas seepages, Giza Pyramids Plateau, Egypt." That title speaks of seeping hydrocarbon gas, and the first telling speaks of hydrogen sulfide. He tells it because underground gas and tunnels would fit his idea that the pyramids were built to use something coming up from below.
